questions.question: Many-shot jailbreaking (MSJ) works by exploiting which property of modern frontier models?
options: Their tendency to follow the last instruction in a long prompt
Their large context windows — constructing hundreds of faux user-assistant compliance turns before the target query causes the model to continue the pattern
Their reliance on system-prompt instructions that can be overridden by sufficient repetition
Their tendency to give shorter answers when the prompt is long
questions.explanation: MSJ fills the context window with fake user-assistant exchanges where the assistant complies with harmful requests, then appends the real target query. The model extracts the compliance pattern from the in-context examples and applies it to the target. The attack does not require prompt injection — it exploits the model's in-context learning mechanism.

questions.question: Anil et al. (NeurIPS 2024) found that MSJ attack success rate follows which mathematical relationship with shot count?
options: Linear: each additional shot provides equal incremental benefit
Logistic: there is an S-curve that plateaus at high shot counts
Power law: ASR keeps climbing polynomially without a clear plateau
Exponential: each doubling of shots roughly doubles the ASR
questions.explanation: The power-law shape is critical: unlike a logistic curve, there is no plateau. At 5 shots, MSJ reliably fails. It begins succeeding around 32 shots. It is reliable on violent/deceitful content at 256 shots. More shots keep improving ASR on a polynomial curve, matching the same power law as benign ICL.

questions.question: Why is it difficult to defend against MSJ without degrading benign in-context learning?
options: MSJ attacks are indistinguishable from benign few-shot examples at the token level
MSJ shares the exact mechanism with benign ICL — pattern extraction from in-context examples — so any defense that suppresses harmful pattern extraction also suppresses beneficial task learning
MSJ always bypasses perplexity filters, and perplexity filters are the only effective defense for ICL tasks
Benign few-shot examples have higher perplexity than MSJ examples, making them harder to protect
questions.explanation: The power-law shape is identical between MSJ and benign ICL because they use the same mechanism: the model extracts the task from in-context examples. A defense that blocks harmful pattern extraction cannot distinguish it from beneficial task extraction at the level of the mechanism — it must work at the semantic level, which is more expensive and error-prone.

questions.question: Anthropic's classifier-based prompt modification defense reduced MSJ attack success from 61% to 2%. What does this defense do?
options: It retrains the model to ignore long-context compliance patterns
It runs a safety classifier over the full context to detect many-shot structure, then truncates or rewrites the relevant portion before the model processes it
It limits all context windows to fewer than 32 tokens to prevent the attack from accumulating enough shots
It replaces all user-assistant turns in the context with a summary generated by a separate model
questions.explanation: The classifier-based prompt modification defense applies a safety classifier to detect many-shot structure (repeated harmful-compliance pairs) across the full context and either truncates or rewrites those turns. This preserves legitimate few-shot examples while removing the MSJ attack structure.

questions.question: How does MSJ compose with PAIR (from Lesson 12)?
options: They cannot be combined because PAIR requires a short context window
PAIR can be used to find effective attack structure which is then replicated as many MSJ shots, and vice versa — the combination reaches higher ASR than either alone
MSJ replaces PAIR in practice because it is more reliable at lower shot counts
PAIR optimizes MSJ shots by gradient search, converting MSJ into a white-box attack
questions.explanation: Anil et al. (2024) report that MSJ composes with competing-objective and PAIR-style attacks: use PAIR to identify an effective jailbreak structure, then fill many shots with that structure. Stacking reaches higher ASR than either attack alone.

questions.question: At what shot count does MSJ reliably begin to succeed on violent and deceitful content, according to Anil et al.?
options: 5 shots
16 shots
32 shots — begins to work — and reliable success at 256 shots
512 shots
questions.explanation: Anil et al. report: fails reliably at 5 shots, begins to succeed around 32 shots, and is reliable on violent and deceitful content at 256 shots. The power-law curve continues past 256 — evaluations now report ASR curves rather than single numbers to capture the full shape.
